svg.text: Ethan — one service, many doors, many KBs, many hands
One Python process on the laptop. Standard library only. Every arrow crosses a process boundary.
DOORS — every way in. A door never thinks.
Telegram
long-poll, outbound only
allow-listed user ids
Console
live run logs, ingest
CLI — bin/ethan
talks to the console API
--ingest, --state
Backfill
past session transcripts
batch, resumable
each door declares which privacy classes it may reach — doors.json
Router — the only part that knows everything
classify the ask → pick the KB → pull cited context → write the task brief → pick the hand → run → report → offer to keep what was learned
one small LLM call with a strict JSON schema decides: kind · KB · hand · steps · search query. A keyword hint in the ask pins the KB with no call at all.
kinds: question · build · review · chain · followup · chat
The router reasons. It never edits code, never runs a build, never holds a repo open. That is what hands are for.
state in SQLite: tasks · messages · runs · replies · harvests — conversations survive a restart
read + write
spawn per task
KBs — what is known
KB tenants, reached through a thin JSON-RPC client
search · context search · ingest · job status — never the full tool surface
hosted
one tenant per KB
local
never leaves the laptop
kb-map.json holds URL, tenant, ontology, privacy class, writable flag,
routing hints and owned repo paths — and the NAME of a token variable, never a token
adding a KB is adding one entry
Hands — what acts
coding agents started through core in the target repo
claude -p · codex exec · kimi -p — same brief to any of them
two watchdogs, both enforced by the parent: a hard runtime cap
and a silence cap, because a stalled hand prints nothing
output streams to a per-run log the console can watch live
core owns each host command, role policy and hand environment
Two enforced checks and the managed-write target
Privacy wall. A door may only reach KBs whose class it lists. Unknown door, or no classes declared → nothing. It fails closed.
Redaction. Everything bound for a KB passes twelve secret patterns first. A match refuses the write — it does not quietly scrub it.
Managed writes — target. Core brokers outward writes; today the selected KB token still reaches the hand, so unattended grants stay off.
Approvals may arrive through any verified door. Direct host actions remain host-managed.
